Looking at this position, I need to analyze what White has:
- King on f5
- Pawns on g7, h6, and g2
- Two far-advanced passed pawns, with the g-pawn one square from promotion

Black has:
- King on a3 (too far away to help)
- Knight on d7 (just moved)
- Pawns on a5 and b3

**The best move is clearly g8=Q.**

The g-pawn has a clear, unstoppable path to promotion. White must convert it immediately to a Queen. The Black knight on d7 cannot prevent this, and the Black king is completely out of play on a3.

After g8=Q, even if Black tries Nf6+ to give check, White's king simply steps aside (Kg5 or Kf4), and the h-pawn will promote next. White wins easily with the new Queen supporting the h-pawn.

**Coaching note:**
When a passed pawn reaches the 7th rank with a clear promotion square, convert it to a Queen immediately—don't hesitate! Your opponent's pieces can't stop it, and a new Queen is the fastest path to victory. The advanced h-pawn becomes unstoppable once you have the Queen's support.
